newsitem.title: GERMANY: Agfa says sees higher operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Agfa says sees higher operating profit.

text.p: Agfa-Gevaert, the photo and imaging unit of German chemicals giant Bayer AG, said it expects to post a higher operating profit this year as turnover was boosted by a key acquisition.
Agfa management board chairman Klaus Gerlach said on Wednesday evening that this year's operating profit would be around 250 million marks in 1996 after 205 million marks last year.
Sales should be around 7.5 billion marks, a 15 percent increase from year-ago-levels, Gerlach said.

Gerlach said the majority of growth was generated by the printing plate business, acquired from Hoechst AG at the beginning of the year. "Without this business, sales would have grown by 2.5 percent," he said.
For 1997 the group expects further increases in profits and sales.
In 1996 Agfa benefitted from more favourable currency exchange rates. "The stronger the dollar, the better this would be for Agfa," Gerlach said.
The group expects a operating profit of around 350 million marks. Sales will only grow moderately.
Next year some 1,000 jobs are expected to be cut, he added.
